Job Description
Interior Communications Technicians perform, coordinate, monitor, and direct the installation, configuration, maintenance, and repair of electrical,
electronic, fiber optic, electrohydraulic, electromechanical, and synchro/servo systems on ships and at shore facilities including alarm, safety, and warning
systems, auxiliary power and support systems, data conversion and distribution systems, indicating, metering, and ordering systems, Interior
Communications (IC) systems, Audio/Video (A/V) entertainment, communication, and monitoring systems, navigation systems, environmental systems,
and Visual Landing Aids (VLA); conduct network administration and maintenance; and perform Interior Communications (IC) watchstanding.

common_text: Interior Communications Electricians (IC) configure and perform organizational and intermediate maintenance on alarm, safety, and warning systems, auxiliary power and support systems, data conversion and distribution systems, indicating, metering, and ordering systems, Interior Communications (IC) systems, phone systems, Audio/Video (A/V) entertainment, broadcast, communication, and monitoring systems, navigation systems, environmental systems, and Visual Landing Aids (VLA); conduct network administration and maintenance; interpret and analyze ship’s blueprints and system interface diagrams; inspect, test, and make detailed casualty analyses; and direct maintenance and repair of electrical, electronic, fiber optic, electrohydraulic, electromechanical, and synchro/servo systems. __________________________________________ These Occupational Standard is to be incorporated in Volume I, Part B, of the Manual of Navy Enlisted Manpower and Personnel Classifications and Occupational Standards (NAVPERS 18068F) as Chapter 43.

Interior Communications Electricians (IC) configure and perform organizational and intermediate maintenance on alarm, safety, and warning systems, auxiliary power and support systems, data conversion and distribution systems, indicating, metering, and ordering systems, Interior Communications (IC) systems, phone systems, Audio/Video (A/V) entertainment, broadcast, communication, and monitoring systems, navigation systems, environmental systems, and Visual Landing Aids (VLA); conduct network administration and maintenance; interpret and analyze ship’s blueprints and system interface diagrams; inspect, test, and make detailed casualty analyses; and direct maintenance and repair of electrical, electronic, fiber optic, electrohydraulic, electromechanical, and synchro/servo systems. __________________________________________ These Occupational Standard is to be incorporated in Volume I, Part B, of the Manual of Navy Enlisted Manpower and Personnel Classifications and Occupational Standards (NAVPERS 18068F) as Chapter 43.

Interior Communications Technicians perform, coordinate, monitor, and direct the installation, configuration, maintenance, and repair of electrical, electronic, fiber optic, electrohydraulic, electromechanical, and synchro/servo systems on ships and at shore facilities including alarm, safety, and warning systems, auxiliary power and support systems, data conversion and distribution systems, indicating, metering, and ordering systems, Interior Communications (IC) systems, Audio/Video (A/V) entertainment, communication, and monitoring systems, navigation systems, environmental systems, and Visual Landing Aids (VLA); conduct network administration and maintenance; and perform Interior Communications (IC) watchstanding.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
